newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka bourse allows 10 pct swing in share price.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka bourse allows 10 pct swing in share price.

text.p: Bangladesh's Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) said on Friday it was limiting price movement of shares to within 10 percent of previous day's rate to discourage speculative trading.
"No bid for any securities in a day shall be allowed in the Exchange in excess of +/- (plus/minus) 10 percent compared to the previous day's rate," the DSE said in a statement.
It said the new rule would be effective Saturday.
The DSE move came after the market watchdog Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) warned investors on Wednesday not to trade in companies that are in red and avoid transactions in the kerb market.

The SEC warning was prompted by an unprecedented rise in share prices amid euphoric buying by a new brand of retail invetsors, who have been encouraged by the recent political stability in the country.

The SEC has indentified 24 listed companies whose price rise was not backed by adequate rise in assets or earnings. The market reacted to the SEC caution falling two consecutive days before it closed for Moslem Friday weekend.
Market analysts said the market was now consolidating and the downwards trend might continue in the next week.
The DSE benchmark index reached its peak of 2,087 points on Tuesday but slid to 2024.43 on Thursday.
